configures.description: For a workflow under models/: the templates/ workflow this is a tuned per-checkpoint configuration of, as a catalog name such as 'templates/text-to-image'.

shape.description: What the workflow produces. Derived from the steps by the server; declare it only where the derivation is wrong. Closed vocabulary - adding a value is additive, renaming one breaks every client that filtered on it.

traits.description: How the output is made or what it needs supplied. Derived by the server; declare only to override.

summary.description: One line saying what the workflow is for, carried in catalog listings. Defaults to the first sentence of 'description'.

cost.description: Measured runs, one per device the maintainer measured on, each measured at the workflow's variable defaults: a run that moves num_inference_steps, width/height or num_frames off them is quoted scaled in proportion (plan basis 'derived'), so a figure measured anywhere else must be re-priced to the defaults before it is written. Never invented without a run; absent means unknown. 'minutes' is the whole run's wall clock on a worker that has to load the models - what a consumer actually waits through, not the denoise loop alone; on a video template the two differ by minutes.

name.description: The accelerator, for a person: 'RTX 4090', 'M2 Ultra'

scales_with.description: Cost drivers this figure is proportional to beyond the generic num_inference_steps, width/height and num_frames: a scalar driver (a run at twice its default is quoted at twice 'minutes'), or a field of a list driver's entries, summed over them. The model's rule, declared here because the engine knows no model's arguments - a Music 3 'audio_duration' is a ceiling, so a track that ends early costs less than the quote.

fixed_minutes.description: The part of 'minutes' that does not scale with the cost drivers (model load, text encode, VAE decode, a LoRA fuse). A run that moves a driver is quoted fixed_minutes + (minutes - fixed_minutes) x the scale factor, so a long run is not charged the fixed share many times over. Declared by the workflow, set from two measured runs; absent means the whole figure scales.

per_entry.description: For a list-driven workflow: the measured cost of one entry of 'variable' (every member it produces), and the length of the default list 'minutes' was measured with, so a run over N entries is (minutes - per_entry.minutes * entries) + per_entry.minutes * N.

cost_drivers.description: The variables that move this workflow's cost, by name - a frame count, a step count, a segment count, not a prompt or a seed. Runs of this workflow are bucketed by these values when the server reports what its own history observed, so a 141-frame run never informs a 124-frame figure. Each name must be a variable this workflow declares. Declaring none is not neutral: the observed figure then falls back to runs that overrode nothing at all, which most real runs do not.

presets.description: One variable that selects a bundle of other variables' values - a template's quality dial. {selector: {value: {variable: value}}}: the selector is a declared variable whose default names one of its bundles, and every key of a bundle is a declared variable. The chosen bundle sets the variables the caller did not pass; an explicit argument always wins. Bundle values are validated exactly as caller values are.

host_ram_gb.description: Host RAM (GB) a run of this workflow is declared to hold at its peak: a number, or a 'variable:' reference so a presets bundle can set it per tier. The server's host-RAM gate holds the job until the host has that much free beside the jobs already running - including those of other dw.serve processes on the same machine - and refuses it at submit when the host's total RAM could never hold it. A maintainer's reading of the measured peak, the way 'cost' is; a figure the server has observed for the same memory key that is larger wins.

vram_estimate.description: A declared VRAM ceiling over this workflow's cost_drivers, checked against each 'cost' entry's 'vram_gb' in validate_workflow and again before a run starts. Never derived from a profiler - a maintainer's own reading of what a stage needs, the same way 'cost' itself is. Projected per pipeline step of the definition as it will run - variables substituted and every for_each expanded, so each member is projected with its own values: required_gb = base_gb + bytes_per_voxel * (product of voxel_variables' values) / 2^30 + gb_per_reference * (the step's 'references' entries whose from_file/from_previous_result is not null) + bytes_per_guide_voxel * (sum over the step's guides of snapped guide frames) * (product of the voxel_variables other than num_frames) / 2^30; a step projecting above any cost entry's vram_gb for that entry's device is refused, not warned, since the failure this guards is an OOM partway through a run that already spent minutes loading. Only the largest step past the ceiling is reported - for a for_each member, at the list entry it came from. 'voxel_variables' names the cost_drivers whose product drives the estimate - typically width, height and num_frames for a video template.

base_gb.description: What stays resident regardless of the voxel count - everything the pipeline keeps on the device throughout, measured or bounded by a real run.

bytes_per_voxel.description: Bytes of additional VRAM per unit of the voxel_variables' product, calibrated from a real run's reported requirement at a known combination.

voxel_variables.description: Names whose product is the voxel count the formula scales with. Each is read from the step's own pipeline arguments, else from the workflow's variables; a step where one is not a number is not projected.

gb_per_reference.description: GB of additional VRAM per reference the step passes - a reference-conditioned pipeline holds each one's encoding resident beside the latents. Every kind counts once; an entry whose media is null is dropped before the pipeline sees it and is not counted. Absent means references are not in the formula.

bytes_per_guide_voxel.description: Bytes of additional VRAM per guide voxel - an H3 guide is encoded on the target canvas, so each one the step lays in (its own 'guides' whose video is not null, plus the one a continuity 'guide' chain appends) costs its snapped frame count times the product of the voxel_variables other than num_frames. A clip's frames are probed from its header; one that cannot be probed (a previous_result:, an unreadable file) is charged at the step's num_frames, the worst case. Absent means guides are not in the formula.

variable_constraints.description: What each variable's value is allowed to be, by variable name. A rule the engine could only enforce after the weights were loaded costs minutes to discover; declared here it is a free refusal at validation time and a line in the catalog beside the default.

seed.description: Default seed for the entire workflow. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

argument_template.description: Engine-injected: the arguments a parent workflow hands this one when it runs it as a sub-workflow. At run time _sub_workflow_action holds them on the child workflow, and they are never written into the definition. A value authored here is read only when this workflow is not run as a sub-workflow.

variable_constraint.description: A rule the author declares for one variable's value, in the same field names a chain step's 'frame_snap' uses, so a model's frame rule is written once. Checked before anything is queued and reported beside the variable's default, so a consumer reads the rule rather than guessing it (#96).

min_length.description: For a string value: the fewest characters it may have once surrounding whitespace is dropped (a null counts as empty), so 1 refuses an empty string. Put what to send instead in 'reason' - a Music 3 instrumental is a tag-only lyrics body, not an empty one.

required.description: The variable has no default and the caller must give it a value: declare it null in 'variables' and set this true. A run, or a validation that is given 'arguments', refuses it while it is still null, naming the variable and quoting 'reason'; the stored null is not itself judged. Use it where a placeholder default would quietly resolve to something the caller did not choose (a voice to clone).

max_words_per_second.description: For a string value: the most words it may carry per second of the number 'seconds_from' names, warned (validation warning and the job's 'text_may_overrun') and never refused. A [bracketed] tag is markup, not a word. The rate is the workflow's own measurement - music-long cuts a section at its 'seconds', so a lyric longer than that fits loses its last lines; say where the rate was measured in 'reason'.

seconds_from.description: With 'max_words_per_second': the number of seconds the value has, read from the same list entry for an entry field (a section's 'seconds'), else from the workflow's variables. Not a number yet (a reference), the value is not judged.

snap.description: What to do with a value the rule refuses. 'up' rounds to the next value the rule accepts, and warns that it did; absent, the value is refused.

reason.description: Why the rule exists, in the author's words - quoted in the refusal and reported beside the default.

step.$comment: A step is closed: the engine reads only the properties above, so an invented control-flow key ('when', 'retry') or a mistyped real one ('relase_pipeline') is a hard error rather than a silent no-op.

for_each.description: Run this step once per entry of a list. A list, or a 'variable:' reference to one. Inside the step, 'item:' is the entry and 'item:field' one of its fields (or {"item": "field", "default": X}, the field with X for an entry that omits it); a later step reads every member's result with 'gather:<step name>'. Members are named '<step name>@<entry name>' (or '@<index>' for an entry without a name), so '@' is reserved in step names.

seed.description: Default seed for the entire step. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

release_pipeline.description: Unload this step's pipeline once the step completes, freeing its memory for later steps. A later pipeline_reference to this step is an error, and the persistent worker's cross-run model cache will not retain it.

release_models.description: Unload every cached task model once the step completes, freeing their memory for later steps. Task models otherwise stay loaded for the life of the process; set this on a task or sub-workflow step whose model is not needed again, such as a prompt expander running ahead of a generation step. A later step using the same model reloads it.

additionalProperties.description: null declares an argument that is optional - a workflow can expose a variable a caller may pass without inventing a sentinel value for its absence. If a step feeds a required task argument from a variable whose value is null, the document itself still saves and validates - but a run (or a validate/save call that supplies its own arguments) that leaves the variable null fails, since the argument the step needs was never actually given a value.

chain.description: Run this pipeline repeatedly, carrying visual continuity from each segment into the next, and stitch the segments into one long video. Specify the length with one of 'segments', 'match_audio' or 'duration_seconds' ('duration_seconds' overrides 'segments' when both are given).

segments.description: Number of segments to generate and stitch. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

duration_seconds.description: Ask for the chain by its length: the segment count and the last segment's frame snap are derived from this many seconds at the chain's frame rate, and the stitched video and its generated audio are trimmed to exactly this length. Needs 'num_frames' in the step's arguments and a frame rate ('fps' on the chain or a 'frame_rate' argument). Not with 'guide_backoff' or 'carry_pick', which drop frames the up-front plan cannot count. Given beside 'segments', the duration wins and 'segments' is ignored (the run logs it), so a template can offer both with a default segment count. Not with 'match_audio'. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

match_audio.description: Derive the segment count from the duration of this step's hold_audio track, or else its one audio reference, slicing it into frame-aligned per-segment chunks (each segment's hold_audio, or its audio reference); the final video is muxed with the original, unsliced audio track.

continuity.description: How continuity is carried from one segment into the next. 'last_frame' carries the segment's final frame as the next one's keyframe. 'last_segment' carries the segment itself - its frames and the soundtrack generated with them - as a video reference, which keeps motion, camera and voice across the seam instead of appearance alone; it needs a 'segment_argument' holding a references list. 'guide' (MiniMax-H3 t2va and fl2va only - guides stay off ref2va) lays the segment's last 'guide_frames' frames, with their audio when 'carry_audio', into the next at frame 0 as a guide, sets an fl2va keyframe to the guide's first frame, and trims the guide off again; 'trim_frames' and 'carry_frames' do not apply, and 'crossfade_ms' only when 'carry_audio' is false. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

guide_frames.description: 'guide' only - frames of each segment's tail laid into the next as its frame-0 guide, and trimmed off it: 22 or 39 (whole-latent guide lengths), nothing else. Ignored by the other continuity modes. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

guide_backoff.description: 'guide' only - frames, a multiple of 17, to back the carry off from the end of each segment: the next segment is guided by the frames that many before the end, and every segment but the last loses that tail at assembly, so the join lands inside the held copy and each segment's least-constrained tail is replaced by the next take. Not with 'match_audio' or 'duration_seconds'. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

anchor.description: Latent statistics anchor (MiniMax-H3 t2va and fl2va only, with continuity 'guide' or 'last_frame'). 'segment_1' passes segment 1's decoded frames to every later segment as its 'latent_anchor': each later segment's video latent is rescaled, per VAE latent channel, to segment 1's latent mean and std before decode, so colour and contrast stop drifting from segment to segment. Segment 1 itself is not corrected, and audio is never touched. 'none' (the default) anchors nothing; any other value, of any type, is refused naming the two. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

anchor_strength.description: How far each later segment's latent statistics match goes, with anchor 'segment_1' (refused without it): a number from 0 to 1, default 1. 1 is the full per-channel mean/std match; 0 leaves the latent alone; 0.5 moves each channel halfway to segment 1's statistics, holding the look without flattening a deliberate change in light. Anything outside [0, 1], or not a number, is refused naming the range. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

keystone.description: Keyframe source for a guide chain on MiniMax-H3 fl2va. 'segment_1' sets every later segment's keyframe (the 'segment_argument' image) to segment 1's frame 0 instead of the guide's first frame, so each segment is pulled back toward the clean start of the chain; the guide stays the carried tail, and the keyframe region is trimmed at assembly, so segment 1's frame never reaches the output. Needs continuity 'guide': on 'last_frame' the keyframe is the only carry and is refused. 'none' (the default) leaves the keyframe as it is; any other value, of any type, is refused naming the two. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

experimental_capstone.description: Scratch spike (#1187, refused unless DW_EXPERIMENTAL_REFINE_WINDOWS=1), MiniMax-H3 t2va/fl2va: segment 1's frame 'from_end' (default 5) frames before its end is held one latent past every later segment's end as a one-frame guide that joins the forward only once the step's sigma falls below 'enter_below_sigma'.

keystone_slot.description: MiniMax-H3 guide chains with keystone 'segment_1' (#1187/#1188): where segment 1's frame 0 sits in each later segment. 'first' (or null, the default) is plain keystone, the fl2va keyframe at the guide's first latent; 'latent' (scratch spike, refused unless DW_EXPERIMENTAL_REFINE_WINDOWS=1, guide continuity only) writes segment 1's frame-0 latent over each later segment's guide latent 0 for the whole denoise, with segment 1's frame 0 as the keyframe too, and puts the guide's own latent 0 back after the loop; 'last' makes it the fl2va last_image (the step must pass an image and no last_image), which on a static two-minute take held the backdrop with no reset pop, at the price of the subject easing back to the opening pose at each segment's end (bench/records/structural.md, *Keystone slot*); {frame, enter_below_sigma?} a one-frame guide at that frame (a multiple of 17, past the guide's frames), joining the forward only below the sigma gate when one is given (the gate refused unless DW_EXPERIMENTAL_REFINE_WINDOWS=1). With 'last' or a frame the keyframe is the guide's first frame again. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

experimental_latent_carry.description: Scratch spike (#1150, refused unless DW_EXPERIMENTAL_REFINE_WINDOWS=1), MiniMax-H3 guide chains: each later segment's guide takes the previous segment's own final latents (its guide_frames tail, video and generated audio) as condition rows in place of decoding and re-encoding those frames. Needs continuity 'guide'; refused with look_hold or a nonzero guide_noise. A chain holding its track (match_audio, a step hold_audio) carries the video latents only. False or null is off.

anchor_every.description: Scratch spike (refused unless DW_EXPERIMENTAL_REFINE_WINDOWS=1): the keystone and the experimental_capstone apply only on later segments whose 0-based index i has i % anchor_every == 0 (3: indices 3, 6, 9). A whole number of at least 1, default 1 (every later segment); refused on a chain with neither keystone 'segment_1' nor experimental_capstone. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

carry_pick.description: Continuity 'last_frame' only, any model family: pick the next segment's keyframe as the sharpest of the segment's last N frames (variance of a 3x3 Laplacian on luma; ties go to the latest) instead of always the last, so a motion-blurred final frame does not pass its softness on. The segment is trimmed after the picked frame, so motion continues from it; the last segment keeps its tail, and the job log names the picked frame per seam. {'sharpest': N} with N a whole number from 1 to 8 (1 is the last frame); anything else, or any continuity but 'last_frame', is refused naming the allowed values.

look_hold.description: Hold a long chain's look to its first segment with pixel-domain corrections applied to each later segment's decoded frames before its carry is taken, so the carried keyframe and the stitched video are the corrected frames (any model family; segment 1 is the reference and is left as rendered). 'pickup' grades the segment's opening to the carried frame by quantile LUT and carries the mapping to its last frame; 'creep' eases a rise in contrast or saturation back to segment 1's by the last frame, never brightening or touching a darker or paler shot; 'texture' eases faint texture (not edges) back to segment 1's, by at most half; 'precompensate' divides the carried keyframe's contrast and saturation by the boost measured so far (the running mean of rendered opening over fed keyframe, clamped to 1..1.25). true turns all four on; an object picks. 'pickup' and 'precompensate' work on one carried keyframe, so need continuity 'last_frame' (true alone skips them on a guide or last_segment chain, an explicit true there is refused). Absent or false = off, and the chain is unchanged.

check.description: Check each segment before keeping it, any model family: after the first, its seam against the previous segment (the picture jump and the look step, measured as analyze_seams measures them) and its fine-band texture against segment 1's. true uses the default ceilings; an object overrides any of 'jump_ratio_max', 'look_ratio_max', 'texture_ratio_max' (a number above 1 bounding the ratio both ways, or null to skip it) and 'cut_ratio_max' (the largest frame step inside the segment over its typical step - a cut a few frames after the seam; null skips it); and 'audio_dbfs_min' (the floor, in dBFS below 0, of the segment's generated audio as kept; default -70, null skips it, and it is never measured when the chain holds its audio); 'words_similarity_min' (a number above 0 and at most 1, or null, the default: the least similarity of what Whisper hears in each segment's kept audio to its expected line - 'lines', else the segment's prompt's <d> dialogue; a segment with no line records words null and is not re-rolled for it, and it is never measured when the chain holds its audio); 'face_drop_max' (a number above 0, or null, the default: the most a segment's median face similarity to segment 1's frame 0 may fall below segment 1's own) - warn-only, measured and recorded on each shot's 'check' always, failing a segment without a re-roll only when set. Lip sync is not a segment check: judge it by eye, or measure a take with the measure_lip_sync task. A failed segment is re-rendered up to 'retries' times. Segment 1 has no seam and is checked for its audio level, and its words when 'words_similarity_min' is set. Absent or false = off, and the chain is unchanged. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

lines.description: The line each segment is expected to speak, one string per segment, in order, for the words check ('check' with 'words_similarity_min'); unlike 'prompts', the last is not repeated, so it must hold exactly one per segment. Segment k's line is lines[k], else the <d> dialogue of its prompt in 'prompts' (the last repeating), else of the step's 'prompt'; an empty string is no line. Nothing else reads it, and validate warns when the words check is off. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

retries.description: With 'check' on, how many times a segment that fails its check is re-rendered from the same carry, each at a new seed (the step's seed plus the attempt number times 1000003): 0 to 3, default 0. When every attempt fails, the chain keeps the attempt with the fewest failed measures (then the lowest jump; among attempts failing only their words, the highest similarity), records 'check_failed' on its shot, warns and finishes. A cost estimate quotes the worst case. Above 0 without 'check' is refused. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

segment_argument.description: The pipeline argument the carry-over lands in - e.g. 'image' for image-to-video pipelines, or 'references' for reference-conditioned modular pipelines, where the carry-over is appended as an image or video reference.

carry_frames.description: 'last_segment' only - carry just this many frames from the tail of each segment rather than all of them, cutting the reference's soundtrack to the same span. A shorter carry costs less sequence length and memory (MiniMax H3 conditions on reference clips of 2 seconds and up, i.e. 48 frames at its 24 fps). Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

carry_audio.description: 'last_segment' and 'guide' - whether the carry brings the soundtrack generated with it, which is what carries a voice across the seam (a guide holds it, so the seam is not crossfaded). Turn it off when the segments are already conditioned on a supplied audio track, as in a 'match_audio' chain.

trim_frames.description: Frames removed from the head of every segment after the first (an image-to-video segment reproduces its keyframe as frame 0). Also bounds the audio crossfade window to trim_frames / fps seconds. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

crossfade_ms.description: Equal-power crossfade applied to generated audio at segment boundaries, clamped to the trim_frames / fps window. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

fps.description: Frame rate used for the chain's audio math - trimming, crossfading, and match_audio planning. Defaults to the pipeline's 'frame_rate' argument when present; pipelines with a fixed rate (MiniMax H3: 24) need it set here. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

frame_snap.description: Constraint the pipeline places on num_frames - counts must equal modulus * n + remainder within the bounds (MiniMax H3: modulus 17, remainder 5, min 124, max 345). Used to snap the final match_audio segment to a valid length. May instead be the string 'constraint:<variable>', naming an entry of the workflow's 'variable_constraints' - so the rule is stated once rather than twice in one file.

prompts.description: Per-segment prompt overrides; segment i uses prompts[min(i, len(prompts) - 1)]. Accepts a 'variable:' reference; a variable left null leaves every segment on the step's own 'prompt'.

save_segments.description: Write each completed segment to the output directory as a playable mp4 and free its frames, bounding memory to one segment - a crashed chain leaves the finished segments behind. The final video is streamed from the segment files. Requires PyAV and a frame rate. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

keep_segments.description: Leave the segment files in place after the final video is written (default: they are removed once it saves successfully). Only meaningful with save_segments. Each kept file is named on the take's shots ('segment_file'), which is how repair-segment finds them. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

resume_from.description: Resume a chain that died part way: an 'output:' reference naming one segment file an earlier run of the same chain left (<prefix>.<n>.segment-NNN.mp4; the failed chain's 'chain_resume_hint' warning quotes the first). That run's finished segments become segments 1..k and only k+1..N render. Each kept file must hold the frames the plan puts on the timeline for its segment, or the run is refused naming the segment: a resume never changes the plan. The files are copied, not moved, into this run's spill. Needs save_segments true and continuity 'last_frame' or 'guide'; a guide resume's first seam carries the decoded audio, and under experimental_latent_carry the decoded frames encoded again in place of the carried latents, which the 'chain_resumed' warning says. A bare path is refused. Null or absent is no resume. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

stop_after.description: Render a probe of the take: the plan stays the full take's (the same segment count, num_frames and guide grid), but only its first N segments render, and the take is muxed with the match_audio track cut to the rendered frames. The run logs 'chain_stopped_after'; each shot carries 'planned_segments'. A whole number of at least 1; at or past the plan's count the whole take renders. Needs save_segments and keep_segments true: a second run of the same chain with stop_after cleared and resume_from naming the probe's last segment file continues it at segment N+1. A resume that keeps N or more segments with stop_after still N is refused before anything is copied. Null or absent renders the whole take. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

remote_text_encoder.description: Encode prompts with a remote text-encoder service instead of loading the text encoder locally. The pipeline's text_encoder is set to None, the prompt is POSTed to the service (authenticated with the HuggingFace token), and the returned embeddings are passed to the pipeline as prompt_embeds. Mutually exclusive with prompt_weighting.

url.description: URL of the remote text encoder endpoint, e.g. a HuggingFace inference endpoint.

seed.description: The seed for this pipeline. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

additionalProperties.description: Any other key names a pipeline component to load. Diffusers grows component names faster than this schema does, so a key whose value is a component definition - an object carrying 'from_pretrained_arguments' - is loaded under that name. Anything else is a mistyped or misplaced key and is refused rather than ignored.
additionalProperties.unknownPropertyMessage: the engine reads the properties this object declares, plus any other key whose value is a component definition (an object carrying 'from_pretrained_arguments') - anything else would be silently ignored

exclude_from_cpu_offload.description: Component names (e.g. 'vae', 'text_encoder') to keep resident on the accelerator instead of offloading. Only applies when offload is 'sequential'.

device.description: The device to run this pipeline on, e.g. 'cuda', 'cuda:1', 'mps' or 'cpu'. Defaults to the device dw is running on and becomes the default for this pipeline's components. A backend this machine does not have is translated to the one it does, with a warning, so a workflow written on a CUDA box runs on a Mac and back again - the index is dropped in that translation. A 'cpu' device is never translated.

component_type.description: The python type of pipeline to use in the format 'module.typename' module defaults to diffusers

no_generator.description: Whether to use a generator for the pipeline. Some pipelines do not support generators.

enable_attention_slicing.description: Whether to enable attention slicing for the pipeline to reduce memory usage.

disable_attention_slicing.description: Turn off the attention slicing MPS applies automatically. Worth setting for SDXL-family models on a Mac: MPS SDPA is fast at their head dim (64) and slicing made it 2.4x slower.

attention_backend.description: The attention backend to use for the pipeline. 'sparse' is dw's own, not a diffusers backend: comfy-kitchen sparse attention on a MiniMax-H3 transformer's generated-video rows, installed for this call only, with everything else dense. It needs CUDA sm_80+ and bf16/fp16, and runs dense with a warning where it cannot run; on a pipeline with no MiniMax-H3 transformer it also runs dense with a warning (#931).

sparse_tau.description: The sparsity threshold for attention_backend 'sparse': higher is sparser and faster, lower is closer to dense. Defaults to 0.5. A runtime setting like a LoRA scale - changing it reuses the loaded pipeline (#931). Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

sparse_topk.description: sol_attn's top-k routing for attention_backend 'sparse': keep this fraction of key tiles per query tile (strictly between 0 and 1) and drop the rest, the selection lightx2v's SLA LoRAs were trained against. When set, sparse_tau is ignored; unset (the default) routes by sparse_tau. A runtime setting like a LoRA scale - changing it reuses the loaded pipeline (#932). Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

prompt_weighting.description: Enable A1111-style prompt weighting syntax: (word:1.5) for emphasis, [word] for de-emphasis, ((word)) for nested weighting. Also supports prompts longer than 77 tokens. Currently supports Flux pipelines. Mutually exclusive with remote_text_encoder.

pre_load_modules.description: List of Python modules to import before loading the pipeline. Used for modules that register with diffusers on import (e.g., sdnq).

load_components.description: Arguments passed to a modular pipeline's load_components() - modular pipelines load their component weights separately from their config. Use 'dtype' to set the component dtype and 'names' to load a subset of components.

names.description: Names of the components to load. All components are loaded when omitted.

dtype.description: The torch dtype to load components in, e.g. 'torch.bfloat16'

quantization_config.description: Quantization configuration per component, keyed by component name (e.g. 'transformer', 'text_encoder'). A component not named here loads unquantized.

remove_blocks.description: Names of top-level blocks to pop off a modular pipeline's block graph once it is built (blocks.sub_blocks.pop). For a block that always runs and has no input that turns it off: FLUX 3 Klein's 'prompt_upsampler' rewrites every caption and needs an 18.8 GB component, so its workflows remove it and use an explicit upsample step instead (#1168). A name the pipeline has no block for is an error.

configs.description: Values a modular pipeline's blocks declare and read while they run - not components, and not call arguments. Keys are whatever the pipeline itself declares, so what may be set here depends on the model: MiniMax-H3 declares 'canvas_short_edge', 'canvas_max_pixels' and 'reference_image_short_edge'. A name the pipeline does not declare is an error rather than a setting that quietly did nothing.

components.description: Configuration applied to components once the pipeline has loaded them. This is where a modular pipeline's components are placed, since it pulls their weights itself. Keys name a component, optionally as a dotted path into one, e.g. 'text_encoder.model'.

device.description: The device to move this component to, e.g. 'cuda'. Only for components small enough to stay resident - the offloaded ones are placed by their own hooks.

residency.description: Whether the component stays on its device for the whole run ('resident', the default) or rests in system memory and is moved to the device only while one of its own calls runs ('on_demand'). Use on_demand for a component that is large but called a handful of times, like a VAE that only encodes references and decodes the result - it frees the device for the rest of the run and, unlike group_offload, moves the model whole, so a tiled decode costs one pair of transfers rather than one per tile. Not for a component called every step, and cannot be combined with group_offload.

enable_tiling.description: Enable tiled decoding on this component, for a decoder that is not the one named 'vae' (which the pipeline-level 'vae' block covers) - LTX-2.5's 'diffusion_decoder', say, which otherwise decodes the whole video volume in one allocation. 'true' uses the model's own default tile size; an object passes tile and stride sizes through to enable_tiling(), which is what a card smaller than those defaults needs.

attention_backend.description: Pin this component's attention backend persistently via set_attention_backend, e.g. 'flash', 'sage', '_flash_3_hub'. Use this instead of the pipeline-level attention_backend when the component is compiled - the per-call context manager forces recompiles. 'sparse' installs dw's comfy-kitchen sparse attention on a MiniMax-H3 transformer instead of calling set_attention_backend, and stays installed until the component is configured with another backend; on any other component it runs dense with a warning (#931).

sparse_tau.description: The sparsity threshold for this component's attention_backend 'sparse': higher is sparser and faster, lower is closer to dense. Defaults to 0.5. A runtime setting like a LoRA scale - changing it reuses the loaded pipeline and is re-applied to it (#931). Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

sparse_topk.description: sol_attn's top-k routing for attention_backend 'sparse': keep this fraction of key tiles per query tile (strictly between 0 and 1) and drop the rest, the selection lightx2v's SLA LoRAs were trained against. When set, sparse_tau is ignored; unset (the default) routes by sparse_tau. A runtime setting like a LoRA scale - changing it reuses the loaded pipeline (#932). Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

attn_processor_type.description: The attention processor this component runs, by type name, constructed with no arguments and handed to set_attn_processor(). The pipeline-level 'unet' and 'transformer' blocks cover those two components; this covers any other one that carries attention - LTX-2.5's 'diffusion_decoder', whose default processor is a portable FlexAttention fallback rather than the NATTEN path the decoder was built around.

truncate_layers.description: Drop the tail of a ModuleList inside this component that the run never reads, before any offload hooks are installed. Keys are dotted paths relative to the component, values the number of entries to keep. For an encoder used for its hidden states: MiniMax-H3 conditions on hidden_states[50] of its 64-layer Qwen3-VL, so { 'language_model.layers': 51 } drops the 13 layers whose output nothing consumes while leaving hidden_states[50] bit-identical (keeping only 50 would hand back the final-norm output instead, a different tensor).

remove_modules.description: Dotted paths to modules inside this component that the run never calls, each replaced with an Identity before any offload hooks are installed - a language-model head on a model used as an encoder, say. The attribute survives for anything that looks it up; the weights are freed rather than held (and, offloaded, pinned) for a call that never comes.

preserve_device_placement.description: Whether to leave the component where it loaded rather than moving it to the device. Needed when the component is loaded already placed - by a 'device_map', or by a quantization that pins its tensors to one device. A 'components' block that group offloads already keeps the pipeline off the device on its own. Renamed from 'do_not_send_to_device', which is no longer recognized.

components_manager.description: Attach a ComponentsManager to a modular pipeline. The manager tracks the pipeline's components and, with auto CPU offload enabled, keeps only the running ones on the device. It replaces 'offload', which modular pipelines do not support.

enable_auto_cpu_offload.description: Move components between the device and system memory as the pipeline runs. Requires a device that reports free memory (CUDA). When enabled the manager owns device placement, so the pipeline is not moved to the device directly.

memory_reserve_margin.description: Device memory to keep free when deciding what to offload, e.g. '3GB'

sdnq_optimize.description: List of pipeline component names to apply SDNQ quantized matmul optimization to (e.g., ['transformer', 'text_encoder']). Requires sdnq package and CUDA/XPU hardware.

cache.description: Enable diffusers built-in cache acceleration on the transformer. Hooks auto-reset between inference runs. Accepts a 'variable:' reference to a whole cache object; a variable that resolves to null means no cache, and the object it resolves to is checked against this shape at validate.

type.description: Cache algorithm: first_block (simplest, broadest support), faster (video-oriented, experimental), mag (magnitude-based, needs num_inference_steps), taylorseer (Taylor series approximation), text_kv (text key-value cache).

threshold.description: Cache threshold for first_block and mag types. Higher = more speedup, more quality loss. first_block default: 0.05, mag default: 0.06. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

num_inference_steps.description: Required for mag cache type. The transformer forwards the call runs: the pipeline's num_inference_steps, except where the scheduler runs fewer (MiniMax-H3 runs one fewer, so a calibration reports one ratio fewer than the call's steps; set this to the count reported).

max_skip_steps.description: Max consecutive skippable steps for mag cache. Default: 3.

retention_ratio.description: Fraction of initial steps where skipping is disabled for mag cache. Default: 0.2.

mag_ratios.description: Per-step magnitude ratios for mag cache. Required unless calibrate is true, and checkpoint-dependent. Either a preset name shipped by diffusers ('flux') or an explicit array of per-step ratios. Interpolated automatically when its length differs from num_inference_steps.

calibrate.description: Run mag cache in calibration mode: skip nothing, and report the magnitude ratios for this model at the end of the run as a job warning and log event, so they can be pasted into mag_ratios. Under classifier-free guidance run as separate cond and uncond passes two lists are reported, labeled [cond] and [uncond]; use the cond one. A pipeline whose transformer does not support enable_cache() (a UNet such as SD 1.5, Z-Image) runs uncached with a job warning and reports nothing. Default: false.

cache_interval.description: Full computation every N steps for taylorseer cache. Default: 5.

max_order.description: Taylor series order for taylorseer cache. Higher = better approximation, more memory. Default: 1.

is_guidance_distilled.description: For faster cache: set true when the model is guidance-distilled (FLUX.1-dev, FLUX.1-Krea-dev), where guidance_scale is an embedding and the transformer sees a batch of 1, not a cond/uncond pair. Without it faster fails at the first step with 'tuple index out of range'. Default: false.

enable_slicing.description: Decode the latent batch one sample at a time rather than all at once - the answer to a decode that runs out of memory on a batch the denoise itself fitted. Costs nothing but the loss of batched decode parallelism.

enable_tiling.description: Decode in tiles rather than in one allocation, for a single sample too large to decode whole - a long or high-resolution video, where the peak is the decode rather than the denoise. Combines with 'enable_slicing'.

attn_processor_type.description: The type name of an attention processor

inversion.description: Run the pipeline's invert() rather than the pipeline itself, returning the inverted latents. Only for pipelines that have one.

generate.description: Run the pipeline's generate() rather than the pipeline itself, returning the generated ids. Only for pipelines that have one, such as a conditioner used on its own.

shared_components.description: The names of components this step loads and later steps may reuse. A modular pipeline is given them after it is built, so the components it shares are the ones it actually loaded.

reused_components.description: The names of components an earlier step shared, reused here instead of being loaded again. A reused component keeps the device placement the step that shared it gave it.

shift.description: Exponential sigma shift applied to this scheduler's schedule, for schedulers that take one (MiniMax H3: 12.0 for video, 3.0 for audio in the released checkpoint). Lower it when running few steps - a high shift packs the whole grid near sigma 1 and leaves one enormous final step, which a short schedule cannot absorb. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

device.description: The device to load this component onto, e.g. 'cuda', 'cuda:1', 'mps' or 'cpu'. Defaults to the device its pipeline runs on. A backend this machine does not have is translated to the one it does, with a warning.

component_type.description: The python type of pipeline component to use in the format 'module.typename' module defaults to diffusers

model_name.description: The huggingface hub name of the ip adadapter model to use.

weight_name.description: The file name of the ip adapter weights.

subfolder.description: The subfolder location of a model file within a larger model repository

scale.description: The scale factor of the ip adapter.

model_name.description: The huggingface hub name of the lora. Null switches the entry off: it is not loaded and the step runs without it, which is how a caller drops a template's adapter by passing its model_name variable as null. A step-distillation (turbo) lora sets the step count and schedule the step runs at, so raise those with it.

weight_name.description: The file name of the lora weights.

subfolder.description: The subfolder location of a model file within a larger model repository

scale.description: The scale factor of the lora when fusing. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

alpha.description: The network alpha to scale this lora by, overriding the one its checkpoint declares. peft scales an adapter by 'scale * alpha / rank', taking alpha from the file - a per-module '.alpha' tensor, else a '__metadata__' alpha where the loader honors one, else the rank itself. State it only where the checkpoint's own figure is not the one it was trained at - read the file's header first; the MiniMax-H3 turbo LoRAs each record the right one. Accepts a 'variable:' reference.

adapter_name.description: The user defined name of the adapter to pass to set_adapters function

from_pretrained_arguments.description: Arguments to pass to the from_pretrained function when creating the component. Names at most one source: 'model_name', 'from_single_file' or 'task'. A pipeline assembled entirely from components an earlier step shared and components declared beside it - LTX-2's latent upsampler, say - names none of them and is constructed directly from those components.

model_name.description: The huggingface hub name of the pretrained model to load

from_single_file.description: Location of a checkpoint model from a single file

task.description: The name of a task that transformers.Pipeline understands

torch_dtype.description: The dtype to load the weights as, e.g. torch.bfloat16 - or diffusers' per-component form, an object from component name to dtype, e.g. {"default": "torch.bfloat16", "audio_vae": "torch.float32", "vocoder": "torch.float32"}. 'default' applies to every component the object does not name; without it those load as torch.float32. Each value must name a dtype: a {}-escaped value is refused.

task.$comment: Closed - see 'step'. A task's own arguments are open; it is the task object itself that is fixed.

path.description: The workflow this step composes: a catalog name as list_workflows reports it (with or without '.json'), a path relative to the workflow that names it ('../models/x.json'), or 'builtin:name.json' for one of the packaged fragments. A name is resolved first beside the referencing file, then against this run's own workflows directory, then against each read-only source on the server's search path - so a stored template can be composed without copying it into the workspace. A path outside every source is refused. When the composing step declares a 'result', that is where the composed output is saved and the composed workflow's own last step does not save it again.

content_type.description: The content type of the result when serialized to disk. Audio can be written as 'audio/wav', 'audio/flac', 'audio/mpeg' (mp3), 'audio/ogg' or 'audio/opus'. Opus is written into an ogg container and only encodes sample rates of 8000, 12000, 16000, 24000 or 48000.

file_base_name.description: The base name for saving result and metadata files. It replaces the name the engine would derive from the workflow and step - it is not a prefix on one - so a caller that sets it can predict the file name. That derived name is what makes two steps' files distinct, so give each step that sets one a different value, or the second collides and gets a '-2' counter. A name, not a path - it may not contain a separator; to place a step's files in a subfolder of the run directory set 'subfolder'. The file extension is determined by context and content_type.

subfolder.description: A subfolder of the run directory this step's files are written into, as a relative path like 'final' or 'shots/act-1'. Optional: without it the files land at the root of the run directory as they always have. By convention a step whose output the user will be shown is 'final' and everything else is 'intermediate', which is how a consumer tells the deliverable from the scratch files without knowing the workflow; the engine treats no name specially. May be a 'variable:' or, inside a for_each step, an 'item:' reference. Each segment must start with a letter, digit or underscore; '..' and '\' are refused.

role.description: What this step's files are to whoever looks at the run: 'final' (a deliverable) or 'intermediate' (made for a later step). Optional: without it a subfolder named 'final' or 'intermediate' decides, else a step a later media-writing step consumes is intermediate and every other step is final. May be a 'variable:' reference.

fps.description: Frames per second - only used when output is video. Defaults to the rate the frames themselves carry (a chain's 'fps', a join's own rate, the rate of the file a task read) and to 8 only when nothing knows better. Set it to write at a rate other than the source's - a deliberate slow motion - which the run then warns about. May be a 'variable:' or, inside a for_each step, an 'item:' reference, resolved the same way 'subfolder' is - the resolved value must be a positive number; a fractional rate (23.976, 29.97) is written as the exact rational (24000/1001, 30000/1001).

sample_rate.description: Audio sample rate - only used when output is audio

audio_sample_rate.description: Sample rate of the audio generated with a video, muxed into 'video/mp4' output. Defaults to the rate reported by the pipeline's vocoder - only set this to override it.

subtype.description: Audio encoding subtype, e.g. 'PCM_24' for wav and flac or 'VORBIS' for ogg. Defaults to the container's own default ('PCM_16' for wav and flac). Only used when output is audio.

compression_level.description: Encoding compression level from 0.0 to 1.0 for compressed audio formats (flac, mp3, ogg). Higher means smaller files. Only used when output is audio.

bitrate_mode.description: Bitrate mode for compressed audio formats: 'CONSTANT', 'AVERAGE' or 'VARIABLE'. Only used when output is audio.

embed_metadata.description: Whether to embed generation parameters as metadata in saved images (PNG info chunks or EXIF). Only applies to image content types.

format.description: Audio container format handed to the writer, e.g. 'WAV' or 'FLAC'. Derived from content_type unless set. Only used when output is audio.

group_offload.description: Stream a model between system memory and the accelerator a group of layers at a time. Anything beyond the keys named here is passed through to apply_group_offloading, e.g. 'use_stream', 'num_blocks_per_group', 'low_cpu_mem_usage', 'offload_to_disk_path'.

compile_config.description: Compile the component with torch.compile once it is fully configured. Best paired with a pinned attention_backend - the per-call context manager forces recompiles.

fullgraph.description: Require a single graph with no breaks. Fails fast on graph breaks instead of silently losing speedup.

dynamic.description: Compile with dynamic shapes. Set true when resolutions or frame counts vary between runs to avoid recompiles.

repeated_blocks.description: Compile only the model's repeated block classes (diffusers regional compilation) - near the same speedup as full compilation with a fraction of the cold-start cost.
